summary: All round-1 critical and major findings are resolved. The backslash injection fix in escapeMarkdownV2 is correct and single-pass safe: the loop iterates over the original value string, not the output StringBuilder, so emitted escape characters cannot be re-processed. Tracing value '\*' through the new logic produces '\\\*' (Java literal), which Telegram parses as escaped-backslash + escaped-asterisk (two safe literals) — injection eliminated. The HTML double-quote fix adds case '"' -> sb.append(""") which prevents attribute breakout in Telegram HTML mode. The full MarkdownV2 special-char set remains complete; backslash is now handled by the dedicated c == '\\' branch before the MARKDOWN_V2_SPECIALS indexOf check. No new injection paths were introduced by the changes. The added null-precondition on subscriber makes existing NPE behavior explicit without introducing a new attack surface. New regression tests (markdownV2EscapesBackslashToPreventInjection, htmlModeEscapesDoubleQuoteInAttribute) pin both fixes with correct expected values.
